Examine basic concepts of family systems and substance use dependency for supporting families in counseling.
Apply developmental stages and principles of group leadership to planning and facilitating groups.
Prepare and facilitate a group session based on wellness and recovery principles for diverse groups.

rows.title: Music/Art/Literature: Modern
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify modern artistic figures and the aesthetic characteristics of their works.
Synthesize a formal understanding of aesthetics with a personal reaction to the arts to enable an informed response to artistic expression.
Analyze works of art in their historical and cultural contexts through discussion and writing.
Describe the interconnections among various artists, historical movements, and artistic disciplines.
Describe the influence of non-Western cultures on Western artistic movements as well as the ways in which the idea of a Western canon was constructed.

rows.title: Women in the Arts
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and critique established and emergent women artists in various disciplines.
Analyze the relationship between artists and their cultural and historical context of production.
Explain the obstacles and challenges women have faced in establishing themselves as artists.
Compare establishment media with traditional forms to question the distinction often drawn between crafts, with which women have been closely associated, and the fine arts.

rows.title: Comparative Religions
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify core concepts of major religions from around the world.
Compare the world views that major religions represent.
Analyze texts and documentary sources about major world religions.

rows.title: American Cultures in Literature and Film
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply literary and film terminology used in aesthetic evaluation and cultural criticism.
Analyze how the concept of the American dream has shaped cultural formations in the U.S. and beyond.
Assess historical and contemporary issues in the U.S. through cinematic and literary representations.
Evaluate the intersectionality of any two interlinking features of one’s social location as bases of oppression or privilege as depicted in American literature and film.

rows.title: Asian Humanities: Contemporary
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze modern Asian aesthetics as expressed in different ethnic and cultural groups.
Identify the cultural areas of Asia and compare their contributions to the arts of the modern and post-modern periods.
Evaluate Asian cultural transformations within the context of relationships of power expressed through the emergence of local and global artistic trends.
Assess approaches to debates about modernity in Asian and the Middle Eastern philosophies in an era of globalization.
Apply knowledge of the transforming cultural narratives found in contemporary Asian humanities through an original creative project.

rows.title: Introduction to Museum Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the creative and critical perspectives related to the history, design, and practices of museums in the United States in the last 100 years.
Assess the value and variety of the missions of museums in the context of local museum and exhibition resources.
Evaluate multicultural voices and visions in art, history, and science museum collections.
Analyze museum strategies for evoking and synthesizing personal transformation and community engagement.

rows.title: Social Justice Work Experience
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Formulate personal, measurable learning objectives relating to work settings in the social justice, non-profit sector.
Apply the knowledge and the skills necessary for successful job performance in a social justice, non-profit employment setting.
Assess the benefits of the work experience and plan future educational steps to continue to grow in or to transfer to the social justice, non-profit sector.

rows.title: Poetry for the People
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and appraise poetry from different racial/ethnic and social groups.
Compose and revise poems that demonstrate awareness of diverse cultural traditions.
Compare the aesthetic features of poetic traditions and forms from diverse cultures across time.
Design and execute a project that takes poetry to the community.

rows.title: Ways of Faith
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define the foundational beliefs and practices of the world faiths as expressed in their preeminent scriptural writings.
Compare the core beliefs of the world religions and assess how knowledge of these religious systems can serve to advance world peace.
Explain how the symbols and sacred sites of the global faiths are reflected in various artistic traditions.
Analyze the spiritual arts of the major faith traditions through the ages in various cultures.

rows.title: Fa'a Pasefika: Interdisciplinary Cultural Expressions of Oceania
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the centrality of the ocean aesthetic across Pacific Islander cultural practices.
Evaluate artistic and creative works that emerge from the experience of the sea.
Analyze how forms of social oppression shape artistic expressions across Oceania.
Produce works of cultural and artistic expressions that speak to social justice issues.

rows.title: Diversity and Social Justice: Racism
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze racism as a system of oppression and privilege.
Assess biases and stereotypes regarding racism.
Examine individual and collective ways to take action in response to racism.
Explain the intersectionality of racism with other distinct forms of social oppression.

rows.title: Diversity and Social Justice: Heterosexism
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES

outcomes: Describe and analyze heterosexism as a system of oppression and privilege.
Assess biases and stereotypes in relation to heterosexism.
Examine individual and collective ways of taking action against heterosexism.
Explain the intersectionality of heterosexism with other distinct forms of social oppression.

rows.title: Diversity and Social Justice: Class and Classism

Assess biases and stereotypes regarding class and classism.

Explain the intersectionality of class with other distinct forms of social oppression.

rows.title: Diversity: Ageism and Adultism (Age-based Oppression)
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:

Explain the intersectionality of age-based discrimination with other distinct forms of social oppression.

rows.title: Introduction to Residential Interior Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES

Examine and apply residential interior design professional practice techniques and procedures

rows.title: Global History of Interior Design

Compare the characteristics of each design movement and their influence upon other movements and designers.
Identify the characteristics of various historical periods and movements of interior design.

rows.title: Beginning Conversational Italian

rows.title: Continuation of Intermediate Conversational Italian

Explain elements of the history, culture, and social trends of the Italian-speaking world.

rows.title: Elementary Italian

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Italian

Explain and compare elements of Italian culture at an elementary level.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Italian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES

Interpret the main idea of a written text in Italian at an intermediate-high level.

rows.title: Beginning Conversational Japanese

rows.title: Introduction to Contemporary Media

rows.title: Latinas in the U.S./VOCES

rows.title: Introduction to Statistical Methods in Latin American and Latino/a Studies

rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain environmental politics and policy in the United States, including their historical development.
Appraise the role of environmental issues and politics in international relations using International Relations theories.
Compare environmental politics and policy in other countries using comparative political science approaches.
Analyze and express basic concepts of environmental political theory, including ecofeminism and non-Western perspectives.

rows.title: The Politics of Globalization
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze competing theories about globalization.
Explain the impacts of globalization by identifying and comparing the relevant history.
Apply social science methodologies to evaluate how globalization power relations have impacted social and political norms and attitudes.

rows.title: The Constitution and Individual Rights
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the law with a general knowledge of its basic principles and applications.
Distinguish and evaluate the individual's legal rights and privileges and how to protect them.
Compare the various types of law.
Define and analyze constitutional amendments, rights, and limitations.

rows.title: International Relations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare the major International Relations theories, emphasizing realism, idealism, gender, and constructivism.
Explain the organization of the international political system, including being able to identify international institutions.
Evaluate the role of national, international, and subnational actors, including nonstate actors, corporations, and non-governmental organizations in the broader context of lnternational Relations.
Apply International Relations theory to evaluate key contemporary subjects, including security, terrorism, human rights, and global environmental degradation.

rows.title: Abnormal Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Summarize the challenges and benefits in establishing and applying criteria for psychological abnormality.
Evaluate and debate the methods currently used to assess and diagnose psychological abnormality.
Analyze the symptoms and functional impacts of major psychological disorders.
Compare the major theoretical models used to understand the etiology and treatment of abnormal behavior.
Analyze and assess the impact of sociocultural factors on the assessment, diagnosis, and prevalence of mental disorders.

rows.title: Psychology of Shyness
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the behavioral, cognitive, and emotional dimensions of shyness within socio-cultural contexts.
Summarize the research and major theoretical perspectives on shyness and social anxiety.
Apply effective psychological strategies to address social anxiety challenges and to increase acceptance of shyness as a form of temperamental diversity.

rows.title: Psychology of Eating, Food, and Weight
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the biopsychosocial relationship between emotions, cognitions, and behaviors and eating, food, and weight through analysis of current research.
Explain the etiologies, treatments, and cross cultural variations of major eating disorders.
Differentiate and personally redefine common misconceptions related to eating, food, and weight.

rows.title: Research Methods
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain key psychological research concepts.
Apply research methodologies to specific research questions.
Critique research approaches through various lenses.
Summarize guidelines for the ethical treatment of diverse human and animal participants in research.

rows.title: Psychology of Race and Ethnic Relations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the impact of race and ethnicity on affect, cognition, and behavior.
Evaluate current research on the psychology of race and ethnicity.
Analyze how prejudice and racism shape the dynamics of relations across and within racial and ethnic groups.
Identify psychological outcomes associated with racial and ethnic identity.
Distinguish the psychological consequences of racism for both the oppressed and oppressing groups.

rows.title: Psychology of Gender
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate current research and theories on the psychology of gender.
Articulate how gender stereotypes impact self-perception, interpersonal dynamics and mental health.
Identify psychological outcomes associated with gender identities, including interpersonal relationships and the social world.
Describe and evaluate gender-oppressive systems and the resulting psychological impact and methods of response.

rows.title: Social Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe research methods and major scientific studies conducted in social psychology.
Integrate theoretical perspectives and concepts used in social psychology to explain human behavior and mental processes in social situations.
Analyze the ways in which an individual’s thoughts, feelings, and behaviors influence and are influenced by other people, sociocultural factors, and/or aspects of the physical environment.
Apply social psychology to explain everyday problems and real-world issues.

rows.title: Child and Adolescent Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and critically evaluate the various research designs used by developmentalists.
Differentiate the stages of development from infancy through adolescence.
Analyze and explain the different domains in which development occurs.
Evaluate the applicability of the developmental research and theory to diverse groups.

rows.title: Psychology of Psychoactive Drugs
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply basic terms and concepts in psychopharmacology.
Evaluate research findings related to psychoactive drugs for research design, implications and limitations of findings.
Compare the psychological effects of various drug categories.
Debate contrasting perspectives on benefits and risks of drug use and societal drug policies.

rows.title: Introduction to Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate fundamental knowledge and comprehension of major concepts, theoretical perspectives, historical and cultural contexts, and empirical findings within the broad discipline of psychology.

Use a scientific approach (including critical and creative thinking) to understand individuals’ mind and behavior within psychological, biological, sociocultural, and ethnocultural contexts while recognizing that biases filter experiences.
Apply psychological theories, concepts, and values to individual, interpersonal, group, and societal issues to demonstrate awareness of self and others.

Draw logical and objective conclusions about the mind and behavior from evidence to show how psychology evaluates, modifies, and supports its claims and counters unsubstantiated statements, opinions or beliefs.

rows.title: Fire Training Work Experience I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply Firefighter I knowledge and skills to emergency and non-emergency situations.
Analyze dangerous situations and assist with retrieving appropriate tools and equipment for fire personnel.
Use tools and equipment according to the National Fire Protection Association's Standard 1001 for Firefighter I.
Explain the importance of teamwork at emergency incidents and non-emergency training.
Understand that all civilians and patients must be treated equally with respect.

rows.title: Fire Service Work Experience
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply Firefighter One knowledge and skills to emergency and non-emergency situations.

Use tools and equipment physically according to the National Fire Protection Association Standard 1001 for Firefighter One and the California State Fire Marshal Office of State Fire Training Firefighter One standards.
Define the importance of teamwork at emergency incidents and non-emergency training.
Assess patients and use appropriate medical protocols in an emergency response situation.

rows.title: Basic Fire Academy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess patient status and apply the correct basic life support interventions to patients with a variety of emergency medical and traumatic conditions, in accordance with local and national EMT protocols.
Apply job knowledge and performance skills of the current State Fire Training Firefighter One curriculum for firefighting and rescue.
Apply job knowledge and performance skills of the current State Fire Training Firefighter One curriculum for wildland fire fighting.
Apply job knowledge and performance skills of the current State Fire Training Firefighter One curriculum for hazardous materials.
Apply job knowledge and performance skills of the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) and SFFD fire apparatus driving.

rows.title: Incident Command System 300
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the Incident Command System (ICS) organization structure appropriate to the complexity of the incident or event
Explain agency policies that influence management of incidents or events in single or unified command
Develop incident objectives, strategies, and tactics
Implement an incident or event planning process utilizing the appropriate ICS forms
Create an incident plan that demonstrates build-up and expansion, demobilization and closeout of an event or incident

rows.title: Introduction to Homeland Security
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the history of the threat of terrorism and threats to the homeland.
Examine the role of intelligence and counterintelligence within the homeland security discipline.
Analyze the proper steps ranging from mitigation to recovery for all-hazards events.
Describe how the roles of risk communication, warning communication, and crisis communication assist with the mission of homeland security.
Analyze the future role and challenges for homeland security.

rows.title: Public Safety: Emergency Medical Response
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the roles, responsibilities, and medical legal considerations of the Emergency Medical Responder (EMR) in the Emergency Medical Services (EMS) systems.
Apply patient assessment and treatment skills to a variety of emergency medical and traumatic situations within the scope of practice of an Emergency Medical Responder (EMR).
Perform effective interventions for adult, child and infant patients experiencing breathing, obstructed airway, cardio-pulmonary emergencies.

rows.title: Fire Tactics and Strategy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the duties and requirements of the company officer in a fire suppression company on the fire ground.
Apply management principles of operational strategy and tactics in emergency situations.
Explain the skills and concepts applicable to the position of company officer in engine and truck companies and other specialized fire apparatus.
Apply basic knowledge of fire behavior and types of structures and occupancies as they pertain to the role of the company officer.
Identify operational management principles in emergency situations when in overall command of an incident or when working in other supportive command functions.

rows.title: Building Construction for Fire Protection
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the fire resistance of building materials and how it correlates to building classifications.
Compare the different loads and stresses that are placed on a building for possible structural failures.
Differentiate the five building construction types as related to firefighter safety.
Explain the effects of fire and fire behavior on major building systems.
Analyze hazards associated with non-fire caused building collapse and the considerations related to firefighter safety.

rows.title: Principles of Fire and Emergency Services: Safety and Survival
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess whether counseling, psychological, and wellness support programs are appropriate and available for emergency services personnel and their families.
Determine if adopting standardized policies for responding to emergencies can minimize near misses, injuries, and deaths.
Employ concepts of risk management to avoid near-misses, injuries, or line-of-duty deaths.
Evaluate the need for national training standards as they correlate to professional development inclusive of qualifications, certifications, and re-certifications.
Explain how the investigation of near-misses, injuries, and line-of-duty deaths can support cultural change throughout emergency services.

rows.title: Rescue Practices
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Articulate fire service technical rescue apparatus and equipment used in the field.
Identify and describe the basic Incident Command System (ICS) components as they relate to technical rescue operations.
Examine the four tactical phases of technical rescue incidents and the roles of rescue teams.
Identify different technical rescues, associated specialized hazards of each operation, and basic safety practices designed to protect rescuers and the public.

rows.title: Fire Behavior and Combustion
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze why fire starts and spreads
Prioritize the numerous hazardous products of combustion
Differentiate the five classes of fire and their relationship to proper application of extingishing agents
Compare fire control techniques

rows.title: Company Officer 2A: Human Relations Management
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply appropriate human resources policies and procedures that produce company efficiency and successful member performance.
Analyze elements and consequences of the California Firefighters Bill of Rights Act, including disciplinary action.
Apply safety regulations in emergency and non-emergency situations.
Justify key components and consequences of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996.

rows.title: Company Officer 2C: Fire Inspections and Investigations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform a fire inspection in compliance with the policies of the authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) and prepare the proper documentation for recording and initiating the approved corrective action
Describe construction, alarm, detection, and suppression features that contribute to or prevent the spread of fire, heat, and smoke throughout a building
Explain the steps that need to be taken to secure an incident scene to keep unauthorized persons from restricted areas and to preserve evidence from damage or destruction
Describe how to identify the area of origin or point of origin of the fire and make a preliminary determination of the cause of the fire

rows.title: Company Officer 2E: Wildland Incident Operations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Develop an incident action plan involving resource ordering, incident facility location, incident report generation, and apparatus dispatch to sectors of the incident according to the National Fire Protection Association Guideline 1500.
Organize an emergency medical treatment plan for fire personnel based on local emergency medical protocols using the Incident Command System medical plan form 206.
Communicate with supervisors, crew members and other support personnel concerning updated progress reports on changes in conditions, fire behavior, and significant events related to the incident.
Execute wildland fire suppression operations and return resources to service as the incident is mitigated.

rows.title: Introduction to Sociology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Distinguish and interpret the major contemporary sociological perspectives.
Analyze and distinguish the basic conceptual tools of sociology.
Evaluate and apply concepts from areas of sociological interest to current social issues.
Utilize critical thinking and applications from the discipline of sociology to examine real life situations.
Define the techniques of sociological research.

rows.title: Social Work Seminar
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the major components of social work practice in the context of agency roles and functions.
Analyze how core principles from the NASW Code of Ethics inform decision-making in practice settings.
Examine current challenges in human services using critical thinking, problem-solving, and self-reflection.
Analyze personal practice in diverse communities through a lens of cultural humility and non-judgmental inquiry.

rows.title: Sociology of Deviance and Crime
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare major theoretical perspectives on deviance and the sociology of crime.
Apply sociological analytical tools to the analysis of human behavior and methods for measuring crime rates.
Apply theoretical perspectives to the analysis of societal reactions to deviance pursued by institutions.

rows.title: Sex and Gender in the U.S.
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the social construction of sex and gender
Explain variation among sex and gender beyond the binary
Describe the role of sex and gender in shaping social structure and inequalities in the U.S.
Evaluate the interaction between gender, social institutions, and culture

rows.title: Sex, Marriage, and Family Relationships
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Categorize and trace the social forces that shape family structure and dynamics in the United States from its inception to the present.
Articulate the socially constructed meanings of marriage and family, including their related components.
Analyze how major social institutions and practices influence personal choices regarding the institution of family.
Analyze the impact of social characteristics on family practices, structures, and dynamics using intersectional frameworks.

rows.title: Introduction to Cannabis Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Distinguish sociological theories used in the scholarly analyses of cannabis use, regulation, and activism
Identify and evaluate different methodological techniques for studying the impact of cannabis on society and social relationships
Examine how cannabis laws, policies, and dominant social values establish and perpetuate social inequalities
Apply sociological concepts to current, real life situations regarding cannabis and society

rows.title: Elementary Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate in Spanish at a novice-high level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation, and intonation
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at a novice-high level
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of past and present tense syntax at a novice-high level
Articulate aspects of the cultures of the Spanish-speaking world areas and communities

rows.title: Continuation of Beginning Conversational Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply intelligible pronunciation and intonation at an intermediate-mid level when narrating in the present or past.
Apply accurate grammatical structures in Spanish at an intermediate-mid level to describe daily routines, give commands, or speak about past events.
Respond effectively to spoken Spanish with appropriate grammatical forms, accurate vocabulary, and clear pronunciation at a mid-intermediate level.
Explain the differences between aspects of Latin American and Spanish Peninsular culture and traditions by comparing architectural, culinary, transportation, fashion, and technological tendencies.

rows.title: Continuation of Intermediate Conversational Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate effectively in Spanish at an intermediate high level, expressing opinions and contrasting ideas and concepts when confronted with cultural and social aspects of the analyzed works

Analyze several important films from Spanish-speaking countries at an intermediate high level, comparing different technical, artistic, and cultural aspects with an understanding of the value and intentions of creative expression.
Explain socio-economic and cultural aspects of Spanish-speaking countries as presented in films with a broad understanding of social constructs.

rows.title: Elementary Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate in Spanish at a novice-high level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation, and intonation
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at a novice-high level
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of past and present tense syntax at a novice-high level
Articulate aspects of Latin American and Spanish Peninsular cultures

rows.title: Grammar Review and Composition
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Recognize and use complex structures to interact orally in Spanish at near-native level.
Use accurate Spanish grammar, punctuation, and syntax when producing or summarizing texts.
Interpret complex structures and idioms from original media in Spanish.
Describe examples of literary, historical, and contemporary influences in the Spanish-speaking world.

rows.title: Grammar Review and Composition
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interact orally in Spanish applying complex structures, avoiding literal translation and English interference.
Produce a variety of prose using varied Spanish vocabulary, idiomatic expressions, and stylistic resources.
Apply a variety of colloquial and literary language registers in written and spoken Spanish.
Analyze and compare cultural, historical, and social aspects of the Spanish-speaking world.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally in Spanish at a mid-intermediate level with accurate grammatical structures, intelligible pronunciation, and intonation.
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at a mid-intermediate level.
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of Spanish grammar and syntax at a mid-intermediate level.
Compare aspects of Latin America and Spanish Peninsular cultures and societies.

rows.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers 1
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess the grammar and syntax structures of the language by applying them to professional settings.
Communicate in writing with a broad range of vocabulary related to topics of personal, public, and community interest, applying enriched vocabulary and grammar proficiency.
Communicate and express with detail and some organization familiar and new concrete topics using high-frequency structures and personalized vocabulary that facilitate comprehension.
Describe and compare cultural aspects of Spanish-speaking countries as well as Spanish-speaking groups in the United States.

rows.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers 1B
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess the grammar and syntax structures of the language by applying them to professional settings.
Communicate in writing with a broad range of vocabulary related to topics of personal, public, and community interest, applying enriched vocabulary and grammar proficiency.
Communicate and express with detail and organization on familiar and some new concrete topics using high-frequency structures and personalized vocabulary that facilitate comprehension.
Describe and compare cultural aspects of Spanish-speaking countries as well as Spanish-speaking groups in the United States.

rows.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers 2A
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and synthesize Spanish grammar structures and syntax rules using linguistic knowledge, classifying words or concepts according to word order, grammatical use, and writing rules.
Communicate in writing using a range of formal and academic Spanish vocabulary, grammar, and sentence structures, avoiding interference with English.
Express thoughts fully and effectively in personal and public contexts using detailed evidence to support an argument or point of view.
Compare elements of history and culture of the Spanish-speaking countries in the Andean region.

rows.title: Intermediate Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate in Spanish at an intermediate level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation, and clear intonation.
Interpret the main idea of a written text in Spanish at an intermediate level.
Analyze and compose short written communications in Spanish at an intermediate level.
Assess and articulate aspects of Latin American and Spanish Peninsular cultures responsively at an intermediate level.

rows.title: LGBT Voices in Hispanic Society
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze media in Spanish or literary passages in terms of content, plot, style, and cultural context.
Compare LGBT film, media, and literary characters in Hispanic culture.
Classify LGBT character representation and themes in media and literary passages within the larger context of Hispanic culture.
Integrate and apply, both orally and in writing, new vocabulary and introductory concepts of LGBT culture in Spanish.

rows.title: Advanced Spanish: Hispanic Culture and Civilization
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate effectively in Spanish about Hispanic cultures.
Analyze critically significant issues of each chronological period of Hispanic civilization from the Golden Age to the Present.
Identify historical figures and moments of the Hispanic cultures and civilization from the Golden Age to the Present.
Compare Spanish, Hispanic American, and Hispanic cultures from the Golden Age to the Present.

rows.title: Continuation of Intermediate Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally using an extensive range of vocabulary, sentence structures and proper pronunciation at an advanced-low level about social, cultural, and personal topics with a clear concept of human communication and interactions.
Evaluate ideas, arguments, and facts from written authentic sources using analytical techniques to assess the value of human thinking and creations.

Synthesize information by writing short summaries using complex grammar structures and accurate syntax and punctuation supporting ideas and arguments with critical thinking in an effective and meaningful way.
Analyze at an advanced-low level historical and cultural elements and issues from the Spanish-speaking world to interpret and describe societal differences and diverse viewpoints.

rows.title: Introduction to Statistics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess how data were collected and recognize how data collection affects what conclusions can be drawn from the data.
Identify appropriate graphs and summary statistics for variables and relationships between them and correctly interpret information from graphs and summary statistics.
Describe and apply probability concepts and distributions.
Demonstrate an understanding of, and ability to use, basic ideas of statistical processes, including hypothesis tests and confidence interval estimation.
Identify appropriate statistical techniques and use technology-based statistical analysis to describe, interpret, and communicate results.
Evaluate ethical issues in statistical practice.

rows.title: Custodial Training
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and employ responsible custodial management of tools and equipment.
Employ safe handling of hazardous and toxic waste and materials.
Identify and demonstrate appropriate maintenance practices for various floors and carpets.
Select and use safely various automatic cleaning tools.

rows.title: Vocational Foundation Skills--Reading and Writing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply vocabulary to workplace communication
Interpret information and intentions in written instructions
Write instructions or reports to explain tasks, projects and incidents in the workplace
Use references and websites related to employment and jobs
Employ basic technology skills necessary for workplace communication

rows.title: Design Fundamentals
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply visual design elements and principles to organize compositions and create meaning.
Analyze the quality and integrity of design work to evaluate the relationship between the audience, form, content and context.
Employ research, sketching, and ideation techniques.
Revise and improve a design solution using an iterative process, working individually and as a part of a group.
Employ design vocabulary to explain one's design process and outcomes orally, visually, and in written form.

rows.title: Visual Media Digital Skills
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define and use the major components of the Macintosh operating system.
Use font management software to organize and activate digital fonts.
Use industry-standard software to create basic graphics and animations.
Construct and publish basic layouts for print and web.

rows.title: Design Drawing Techniques
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the role and techniques of rapid visualization in design thinking and making.
Employ various design sketching techniques to explore design ideas.
Analyze and discuss the merits of using design drawing techniques for visual thinking.

rows.title: Graphic Design I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply an iterative design process to various design problems.
Select and use elements and principles to convey a specific message to a defined audience.
Identify basic components of typographic form and function.
Create a unified and communicative composition incorporating type and/or image using appropriate techniques.
Appraise and evaluate student work through in-class verbal and written critiques.

rows.title: Information Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify common information design data types and structures.
Design and produce an information design that enhances the viewer's understanding of a complex topic involving multiple data sets.
Collect and analyze information thoroughly and responsibly while providing citations for reputable sources.
Employ critical thinking and communications skills in the development of information design solutions.
Employ and document an iterative design process.

rows.title: User Interface Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Discuss user-centered design considerations for a variety of interactive products and contexts.
Apply information architecture, visual hierarchy, type, color, motion and design patterns to interface designs for a range of products and platforms.
Apply interaction design principles, including associations, affordances, economy of motion, response and flow designs for a range of products and platforms.
Employ critical thinking and communication skills in the development of user interface solutions.
Employ and document an iterative design process.

rows.title: Typography I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Employ typographic terminology, classification and typesetting conventions in design work.
Create layouts demonstrating how legibility, readability, and typographic hierarchy impact the design of effective communications.
Employ an iterative design process in individual and collaborative design activities.
Analyze various design solutions to determine the effect of typography on connotative and denotative messaging within a design solution.

rows.title: Web Production I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Create web pre-production documents, including site maps, mockups, and wire frames.
Evaluate the effectiveness of website projects.
Use industry-standard tools to create web content.
Employ soft skills that define a professional in the industry, including working with others and communicating clearly.

rows.title: Illustrator I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the major components of the Adobe Illustrator user interface.
Construct basic Illustrator documents according to industry best practices in design and illustration standards.
Analyze and reproduce basic Illustrator files using appropriate tools and techniques.

rows.title: InDesign I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the major components of the Adobe InDesign interface.
Construct basic InDesign documents according to industry best practices in typesetting and layout standards.
Employ document components to reproduce and package a document in InDesign.

rows.title: Photoshop I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Construct basic files in Photoshop using industry-standard best practices.
Identify and describe the major components of the Photoshop user interface.
Analyze and reproduce basic Photoshop files using appropriate tools and techniques.

rows.title: Storytelling and Storyboarding
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze different forms of narrative and describe the narrative structure as it applies to storytelling
Analyze the use of storyboards in the creation of narratives
Analyze the content, context, and thematic elements of preexisting texts
Create storyboards from original ideas and scripts
Create individual, detailed narratives and related storyboards.

rows.title: Digital Illustration I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Research source imagery to use as reference for creating illustrations.
Develop original concepts into images that clearly communicate intended messages.
Create original illustrations with both raster and vector-based tools.
Evaluate and critique their work and the work of others using relevant terms and concepts.

rows.title: Portfolio Preparation
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Design and produce a professional online and sequenced portfolio of work matched to their goals
Develop and execute a self-directed timetable for refining and showcasing a series of portfolio projects
Write and design a curriculum vitae appropriate for furthering personal goals
Present themselves and their portfolio in a professional manner

rows.title: Design Studio Practicum I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Employ a structured design process incorporating peer and instructor feedback.
Combine appropriate aesthetic form and content to create engaging and effective communication design.
Demonstrate design and production documentation skills such as time tracking, project summaries, and style guides.

rows.title: Nurse Assistant/Convalescent Care
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the signs and symptoms to be reported of various diseases, disorders, and behaviors among the elderly.
Explain the legal rules and guidelines set by Title 22 and Title 42.
Describe the professional and ethical roles and responsibilities of the nursing assistant.
Describe and report various types of elder abuse.
Perform geriatric and other long term care related to activities of daily living.

rows.title: Nurse Assistant/Acute Care
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Summarize the role of the certified nursing assistant in the acute care setting.
Compare patient needs and appropriate nursing care in long-term and acute care settings.
Apply proper techniques when performing a range of patient care skills in an acute care setting.

Evaluate and provide appropriate patient care for a range of patients found in an acute care setting, including patients with diabetes, cancer, postoperative patients, and patients with problems of the nervous, circulatory, or respiratory system.
Explain the responsibilities of a certified nursing assistant with regards to wound care in an acute care setting.

rows.title: Basic Medical/Surgical Nursing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Differentiate health and illness across the life span and understand the impact of culture on health for appropriate nursing care.
Identify and discuss with geriatric clients the processes and nursing implications of normal aging, death, and physiological and psychological changes.
Apply knowledge of the anatomy and physiology of the gastrointestinal, integumentary, and musculoskeletal systems to identification and nursing interventions for various related disorders.
Compare and evaluate various diagnostic and laboratory tests and provide nursing measures in relation to the test results.
Describe LVN licensure exam expectations and the critical thinking, clinical judgment, and Next Generation NCLEX-PN skills needed for success.

rows.title: Pharmacology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Calculate basic mathematical problems involving fractions, decimals, percentages, and ratios.
Apply the principles of medication administration, including the safe administration of drugs, in caring for clients in various types of clinical settings.
Describe the common classifications, dosages, side effects, and potential adverse reactions of drugs used for the different body systems.
Differentiate the actions and side effects of commonly prescribed medications, including evaluation of the effectiveness of the drugs administered.
Summarize the legal implications associated with medication administration.
Plan appropriate nursing care in administering medications, considering the genetic differences and cultural backgrounds of diverse clients.

rows.title: Intermediate Adult Medical Surgical Nursing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Formulate daily nursing care in response to a range of major medical-surgical disease conditions and apply appropriate nursing interventions to selected patients.
Apply intermediate-level nursing knowledge and critical thinking related to various medical-surgical disease conditions.
Apply intermediate-level nursing and appropriate clinical judgment in caring for diverse clients with different medical-surgical disorders.
Manage safe, intermediate-level nursing care for patients with a wide range of medical surgical disorders.

rows.title: Maternity and Pediatrics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and discuss prenatal care, adaptations to pregnancy, and fetal development and reproductive health issues.
Discuss prenatal, antepartum, and postpartum nursing care, including the risks, complications, and nursing interventions.
Describe the physiology of the different systems of the body and age-appropriate assessment, diagnostic tests, and pediatric diseases affiliated with those systems.
Employ critical thinking and appropriate clinical judgment when identifying and describing nursing responsibilities and interventions for hospitalized children from infancy to adolescence.
Explain the responsibility of vocational nurses to report necessary notifiable diseases and/or conditions to public health authorities.
Discuss cultural differences and their influence on childbirth and the family unit.

rows.title: Clinical and Skills Lab III
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze at least ten (10) of the LVN Department's Standard Steps of Nursing Procedures.
Assemble the appropriate equipment for each obstetric, pediatric, and medical-surgical skill performed, utilizing standard steps for each procedure.
Explain the purpose of each obstetric, pediatric, and medical-surgical skill performed and formulate a related patient teaching plan.
Perform assessment of patients of all ages with a variety of obstetric, pediatric, medical-surgical conditions and assessment of community health needs in diverse healthcare settings.
Perform, discuss, and identify appropriate health needs and teaching based on client assessment in community and clinical settings.

rows.title: Women and Film
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply fundamental terms from foundational feminist film studies.
Analyze female representation from the silent era to today.
Assess film genres, focused on those with potential to challenge traditional gender roles, including comedy and melodrama.
Interpret the work of significant independent, diverse, feminist filmmakers that challenges mainstream representations of women.

rows.title: Introduction to Women's and Gender Studies: Feminism Demystified
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Examine gender, feminism, and women’s studies through an intersectional lens.
Apply feminist theory to social, political, and economic issues.
Evaluate the causes, effects, and systemic structures contributing to gender-based violence
Define, assess, and propose feminist approaches to social change, emphasizing practical applications and community engagement.

rows.title: The Politics of Sexual Violence
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the political, social, and psychological causes of sexual violence, which disproportionately affects women
Analyze the role of major institutions in contributing to and perpetuating sexual violence
Examine how writing can be used to support survivors of violence and transform a rape culture
Evaluate strategies for preventing sexual violence and transforming a rape culture in the context of interlocking oppressions
